title: SSE frame cursor
description: Illustrative shape of a Server-Sent Events frame as delivered on a turn or loop stream. The `id` mirrors the SSE `id:` line — a monotonic transport cursor clients echo back via `Last-Event-ID`/`?since=` to replay events strictly after it. It is NOT part of any event's `data` payload; event names and data payloads are identical across the HTTP (SSE) and in-process bindings. The frame's own event-specific fields ride under `additionalProperties`.

id.description: Monotonic stream cursor (the SSE `id:` line). PINNED to `string` — the `id` is an opaque, lexicographically-orderable token, never a number. ORDERING NOTE: 'strictly after' is defined by lexicographic string comparison of the `id` values, so emitters MUST mint ids that sort correctly as strings (e.g. zero-padded or otherwise fixed-width monotonic tokens); a bare decimal counter like `"9"` vs `"10"` does NOT sort correctly and is non-conformant.
